group: two periodic regions converting into each other
title: What is known about 1RB1RF_1LC1RD_1RA1LD_1RE0LA_---0RC_0LC1RB
description: Proof status of the six-state BB(6) holdout 1RB1RF_1LC1RD_1RA1LD_1RE0LA_---0RC_0LC1RB.
intro: Nobody knows whether this six-state, two-symbol Turing machine halts when started on a blank tape: it is one of the holdouts left open by the bbchallenge project. This page lists what has been established about it, sorted by what each result rests on.
verdict: The question is open. The tape consists of two periodic regions and one to three defects; sweeping right the head turns one region into the other a word at a time (proved in Lean for every state), and the sizes of the regions swing back and forth as the tape grows. The machine can only stop when the head in state D reads two 0s; the C simulator runs 1011 steps without that happening. The motion of the defects has not been worked out.

claims.title: The halting configurations
claims.text: The machine stops exactly when it reads the symbol of a halting transition (E0); the generated statement covers every configuration.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10,000 steps
claims.text: The list simulator of the shared library, proved to agree with the machine's semantics, runs 10,000 steps from blank tape without a halt, evaluated by Lean's kernel.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10<sup>7</sup> steps
claims.text: The same run, evaluated by compiled code.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10<sup>9</sup> steps
claims.text: The C simulator tools/c/triage.c runs 109 steps without a halt; at the end 57,981 cells have been visited and 43,904 of them hold a 1.

claims.title: Growth shape: exp/sqrt
claims.text: Left of the start, the visited part of the tape grows like the square root of the step count, the signature of a head sweeping back and forth across the whole tape and adding a cell or a few at the end of each sweep (a bouncer-like shape) (fitted exponent 0.506). Right of the start it grows like the logarithm of the step count: each new cell costs a roughly constant factor more time, the signature of a counter or of a Collatz-like map whose values are written on the tape (fitted exponent 0.063).

claims.title: The sweeps
claims.text: In each state S, moving right, every copy of a rotation of 111010 becomes the matching rotation of 111110 (A: 111010 → 111101, …), 6n steps for n words.

claims.title: When it halts
claims.text: The machine stops exactly when the head in state D reads a 0 followed by a 0 (D0 = 1RE, then E0 is undefined).

claims.title: No halt in 10<sup>11</sup> steps
claims.text: The C simulator tools/c/tmrun.c runs 100,000,000,000 steps from blank tape without a halt.

claims.title: Two regions, at most three defects
claims.text: Tapes sampled every 10<sup>8</sup> steps up to 4·10<sup>9</sup> consist of the two periodic regions (between 260 and 14,636 words of each) and one to three defect blocks.

claims.title: Does it halt from blank tape?
claims.text: Not known. Whether the swing of the two regions is regular, and whether a defect can ever put 0 0 under the head in state D, has not been worked out.

claims.title: Related holdouts
claims.text: The same tape and head as 1RB1RE_1LC0RC_1RA1LD_1RB0LA_0LC1RF_---1RD at every one of the first 10<sup>7</sup> steps (the tables differ). The same table as 1RB1LD_1RC1RF_1LA1RD_1RE0LB_---0RA_0LA1RC up to renaming, started in another state; no common configuration in the first 10<sup>7</sup> steps of each.

explainer.lede: Nobody knows. The tape of this machine is two repeating patterns side by side with at most three irregular spots, and the head keeps turning one pattern into the other. It has run 10<sup>11</sup> steps without stopping.

facts.text: The only way it can stop, proved in Lean.
No halt in the C simulator.
Irregular blocks in a tape of up to 100,000 cells.

sections.heading: The shape of the run
html: Left of the start, the visited part of the tape grows like the square root of the step count, the signature of a head sweeping back and forth across the whole tape and adding a cell or a few at the end of each sweep (a bouncer-like shape) (fitted exponent 0.506). Right of the start it grows like the logarithm of the step count: each new cell costs a roughly constant factor more time, the signature of a counter or of a Collatz-like map whose values are written on the tape (fitted exponent 0.063).
After 109 steps the tape spans 57,981 cells (40,782 left of the start, 58 right), with a density of 1s of 0.757.
These are measurements of one bounded run, sorted by tools/py/bbtools/triage.py; the macro structure behind them is the next thing to find.

sections.heading: Two patterns that swap
html: Almost all of the tape is one of two six-cell words, 111010 and 111110, each seen at whatever phase it starts. At 4·109 steps the tape is 99,895 cells long: 7,333 words of the first kind, 9,314 of the second and two irregular blocks.

Sweeping right, in any state, the head turns each 111010 into a 111110, six steps a word; Lean proves it for any number of words. The share of the two words swings widely (at 2.9·109 steps only 260 words 111110 are left, at 3·109 there are 7,972), while the tape grows like the square root of the step count.

sections.heading: Open
html: The machine stops only when the head, in state D, reads two 0s in a row. The sweeps never do; a halt would have to come from one of the defects or from a turn at an end of the tape. The plain C simulator runs 1011 steps without a halt. How the defects move, and what drives the swing between the two words, has not been worked out.

sections.heading: Related machines
html: Other holdouts of the list of 608 that are tied to this one. The comparison of tables is exact; everything about runs was checked on the first 107 steps of each machine and is an observation, not a proof (holdouts/related.py, holdouts/related.json).

Same run as 1RB1RE_1LC0RC_1RA1LD_1RB0LA_0LC1RF_---1RD (observed, not proved). At every one of the first 107 steps from blank tape the two machines have the same tape and the head on the same cell. Their tables differ, and no renaming of the states turns one into the other. While they run, the states pair up as A–A, B–B, B–F, C–C, D–D, E–B, F–E (this machine first), which is not one to one. Transitions not used in these steps: this machine never uses E0 and the other never uses F0. Lean proves (lean/Twin.lean in the other machine's folder, lock_or_break, not_halts_of_noBreak) that the two runs have the same tape, the same head position and paired states up to the first break, a configuration where the paired states act differently, and that neither machine halts if no break ever comes. A halt of either machine is itself a break, and the halting transitions of the two do not correspond, so the two are not known to halt together.

Same table as the machine below, started in another state. Renaming the states as shown turns this machine's table into the other one, the halting transition included. The other machine starts in its own state A, which is not this machine's A: its run from blank tape is the run of this table started in another state. These are different runs: in the first 107 steps of each, no configuration of this machine's run occurs in the other, even up to a shift of the tape. So each of these holdouts is its own halting question, and settling one does not settle another.

summary: The tape is two periodic regions (111010 and 111110) with one to three defects; rightward sweeps in every state convert one into the other a word at a time (proved in Lean), the region sizes swing, the tape grows like sqrt(steps). Halts only if D reads 0 0. No halt in 10^11 steps.
